objective.statement: Optional: choose an approach chord before a cadence.
successCriteria: I know an approach chord comes just before the two cadence chords.
I can choose one from I, ii, IV or V that fits the melody note.
I know this lesson is optional.

explanation.text: This lesson is optional. It helps you harmonise a melody, but you do not need it to complete Grade 5, and nothing in it is in the Grade 5 assessment.

An approach chord is a chord before two cadence chords, so that three chords make a short progression: for example IV, ii, V or IV, V, I. At Grade 5 a suitable approach chord can always be found among I, ii, IV and V.
Choose the cadence chords first. Then pick any of I, ii, IV or V that contains the melody note before them.

music.textAlternative: Three chords in C major: IV, ii, V.

steps: The cadence is the last two chords: ii–V.
The chord before them is IV.
demonstration.textAlternative: IV, ii, V in C major.

guided.prompt: In D major, B and C make a perfect cadence. The chord at A comes BEFORE the cadence chords: it is an approach chord. Choose a chord for each of A, B and C (I, ii, IV or V), each containing its melody note, so that B and C make the cadence. (The approach chord may be any of I, ii, IV or V that fits the melody note.)

music.textAlternative: A treble-clef stave, key signature of 2 sharps, 4/4. Bar 1: a note on the 5th line; a note in the 4th space; a note on the 5th line; a note marked A on the 4th line. Bar 2: a note marked B in the 3rd space; a note marked C in the 2nd space.

hints: First choose the cadence chords for B and C. Then pick a chord for A that contains its melody note and is different from the chord at B: a cadence needs two different chords.

feedback.correct: Yes: the approach chord holds its melody note.

mistakes.chord-lacks-melody-note: Each chord must contain its melody note.
mistakes.non-cadential-pair: Cadences are V–I, IV–I, or end on V.
mistakes.cadence-misnamed: Name the last two chords first: V–I perfect, IV–I plagal, ending on V imperfect.
mistakes.wrong-key: Check the key signature and the final note — then build the chords in that key.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. For each marked note, list the chords that contain it, then choose a pair that makes a cadence.
